page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 512.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 132,083.9 and a PassMark CPU score of 123,481.9. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to a PassMark extended instructions score of 158,056.48. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 9,470.27 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 452.95 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance is moderate, as indicated by an average-tier stress-ng single-core score of 2,262.41.

The server demonstrates strong capabilities in multi-threaded operations, achieving 517.51 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 184.13 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. LLM inference speeds for prompt processing are strong, reaching 245.57 tokens/sec on a 7B model, though text generation speeds are average at 27.72 tokens/sec. The lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs represents a tradeoff, making this instance reliant on network-attached storage. Appropriate workloads include large-scale general-purpose applications, multi-threaded enterprise systems, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
